#Module canvas

Canvas 2D (HTML §4.12.5): the 2D rendering context of <canvas> and OffscreenCanvas, drawn by a software rasterizer (package canvas2d) into a premultiplied RGBA8 bitmap that the shell shows as a texture, updated only when the drawing changed. Members shared by CanvasRenderingContext2D and OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D are one function imported under their mixin's name (CanvasState_save...); those of CanvasPath work on a context's current path or on a Path2D alike (CanvasPathTarget). Arguments that are NaN or infinite make a drawing or path call do nothing (the specification's rule); an enum given an invalid string leaves the attribute as it was.

  • colors are CSS color strings, parsed by the browser's CSS parser (currentcolor is the canvas element's color); fillStyle / strokeStyle read back as #rrggbb or rgba(r, g, b, a);
  • pixel data (ImageData) is straight-alpha RGBA8, rows top to bottom;
  • a canvas that drew an image the page may not read (cross-origin without CORS) is tainted: reading it back (getImageData, toDataURL, toBlob...) raises Security;
  • workers have OffscreenCanvas (drawn in the worker's thread; its text is not drawn yet: the shell's fonts belong to the interface thread); functions taking an element answer as for a dead handle there.

Exposed to: Window, Worker. Source: api/canvas.widl.

#HTMLCanvasElement_context2d

CanvasRenderingContext2D HTMLCanvasElement_context2d(HTMLCanvasElement canvas, bool alpha, bool will_read_frequently) raises

getContext("2d", { alpha, willReadFrequently }): the canvas's 2D context, made on the first call (the bitmap is allocated then) and the same object afterwards. alpha false: an opaque canvas (black until drawn on). Quota when the size is over canvas.max_dimension / canvas.max_pixels or the page's canvas memory (canvas.max_page_bytes).

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: HTMLCanvasElement_context2d :: proc(c: ^Call, canvas: Api_HTMLCanvasElement, alpha: bool, will_read_frequently: bool) -> (u64, Api_Error)

#Canvas_encode

Buffer Canvas_encode(u64 canvas, string type, f64 quality) raises

The canvas (an element, or an OffscreenCanvas handle) encoded as type: "image/png", or "image/jpeg" at quality (0 to 1; outside it the default, canvas.encode.jpeg_quality). Security when the canvas is tainted. An empty buffer for a canvas with no pixels (width or height 0).

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Canvas_encode :: proc(c: ^Call, canvas: u64, type: string, quality: f64) -> (u64, Api_Error)

drawImage: source is an element handle (img, canvas, video) or an object handle (ImageBitmap, OffscreenCanvas); form is the number of arguments after the image, 2 (dx, dy), 4 (dx, dy, dw, dh) or 8 (sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy, dw, dh); the unused ones are 0. #Canvas_createBitmap

ImageBitmap Canvas_createBitmap(u64 source, i32 form, f64 sx, f64 sy, f64 sw, f64 sh, i32 orient, i32 premul, i32 colorspace, i32 resize_w, i32 resize_h, i32 resize_q) raises

createImageBitmap(image, sx, sy, sw, sh, options): source as for drawImage, form 0 (whole image) or 4 (a rectangle). The bitmap is a copy of the pixels now, with the full ImageBitmapOptions applied natively: orient (0 from-image, 1 flipY), premul (0 default, 1 premultiply, 2 none — the result stored premultiplied either way; none only affects a source whose alpha is not premultiplied, which never happens for our premultiplied bitmaps, so it is a no-op here and kept for completeness), colorspace (0 default, 1 none — we keep the source sRGB bytes so both behave the same), resize_w / resize_h the wanted output size (0 means keep that axis) and resize_q (0 pixelated, 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high). Not_Found: no pixels yet (the image is not available); Invalid_State: broken or empty image; Index_Size: an empty rectangle or an out-of-range resize.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Canvas_createBitmap :: proc(c: ^Call, source: u64, form: i32, sx: f64, sy: f64, sw: f64, sh: f64, orient: i32, premul: i32, colorspace: i32, resize_w: i32, resize_h: i32, resize_q: i32) -> (u64, Api_Error)
